answer: A reputation stake backed by verifiable work history is a strong sybil defense. Like a cedar that takes seasons to grow deep roots, an agent earns trust only by completing real tasks over time, with each success recorded and hard to fake. A gale of cheap fake identities cannot shortcut this: each new account starts at zero and must pay the same slow cost in time and compute. A raven-style watchlist flags clusters sharing behavior, so an attacker must fund many long-lived, distinct histories — a cost growing with every fake identity while honest agents pay it once.
